title: Dresden's Kupferstich-Kabinett showcases landmark collection of Japanese art
summary: In the exhibition ‘Japan on Paper in Dresden: Utamaro, Hokusai, Hiroshige, and the Graphic Arts of Modernism’, the Kupferstich-Kabinett (Museum of Prints, Drawings and Photographs) of the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden (Dresden State Art Collections, SKD) is showcasing its outstanding and hitherto largely unknown collection of Japanese art. Comprising more than 10,000 items ranging in date from the seventeenth century to the present day, this collection is one of the oldest and most extensive of its kind in Europe. A selection of 160 exhibits are on show – including works by famous woodblock print artists such as Kitagawa Utamaro, Katsushika Hokusai, and Utagawa Hiroshige, as well as some that are on display for the first time. Everyday life and mythology, elegance and wit, fantasy and true-to-life observation of nature – Japanese woodblock prints encompass all facets of life. title: Definitive monograph on artist Sam Taylor-Johnson to explore portraiture and identity
summary: The definitive monograph on the work of internationally acclaimed artist and filmmaker, this book explores Sam Taylor-Johnson's distinctive approach to capturing the essence of the self within her photographic work. “That is what it is to take a photograph – a portrait of somebody. It’s knowing and seeing, in the briefest of ethereal moments, something like a secret you have found. There’s the hit of a button and the steal of an eye, and all the history that belongs to it has been passed on. Gifted and taken.” -- Sam Taylor-Johnson From her earliest self-portraits as a student at Goldsmiths to her intimate film-portrayals of the musical icons John Lennon and Amy Winehouse and the record-breaking adaptation of Fifty Shades of Grey, Taylor-Johnson has consistently investigated the nature of selfhood, using both photography and film to create bold, psychologically rich portraits. title: Archaeologists begin first detailed exploration of El Yesal, one of the largest Maya cities in the Central Lowlands
summary: Hidden beneath the dense tropical forest of Mexico’s Balam Kú Biosphere Reserve, the ancient Maya city of El Yesal is beginning to reveal its scale and history following the first detailed archaeological survey ever conducted at the site. Although researchers have known about El Yesal for years, the settlement had previously received only brief visits. Its remote location in a heavily forested and largely unexplored region of Campeche had prevented archaeologists from carrying out a systematic investigation. That changed during a recent field season led by Ivan Šprajc of the Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts. The project, authorized by Mexico’s Ministry of Culture through the Archaeology Council of the National Institute of Anthropology and History, is examining an area of the Maya Lowlands that remains poorly understood. title: The Block Museum of Art names Ainsley M. Cameron Associate Director of Curatorial Affairs
summary: The Mary and Leigh Block Museum of Art at Northwestern University has named Ainsley M. Cameron, D.Phil. (Oxon.), as Associate Director of Curatorial Affairs, effective September 1, 2026. Cameron joins The Block from the Cincinnati Art Museum, where she most recently served as Director of Curatorial Affairs & Initiatives. "Ainsley combines deep expertise in ancient cultures, Islamic art, and South Asia with an expansive vision that reflects The Block's commitment to global perspectives," said Lisa Corrin, Ellen Philips Katz Executive Director of The Block Museum of Art. "She has regularly woven contemporary artists' voices into her work with historic collections, creating meaningful conversations between the past and the present. Just as importantly, she is a proven mentor who invests in the next generation of scholars. title: Leonard A. Lauder Collection gifts over 1,000 Wiener Werkstätte postcards to Neue Galerie New York
summary: Neue Galerie New York announced today a major gift from the collection of the late Leonard A. Lauder of more than 1,000 postcards produced by the Wiener Werkstätte (Vienna Workshops) during the period 1907-20. The Wiener Werkstätte was founded in 1903 by architect Josef Hoffmann and designer Koloman Moser. In 1907 the Wiener Werkstätte began publishing a numbered series of postcards. Capitalizing on the widespread international craze for the postcard, then a relatively new communications medium, the Wiener Werkstätte promoted these as small works of art that could be accompanied by a brief message and even marketed frames to display them. title: Library of Congress acquires manuscripts, papers and recordings of Rock & Roll Hall of Famer Doc Pomus
summary: The Library of Congress recently acquired the manuscripts, papers, photographs and sound recordings of songwriter Doc Pomus, who was responsible for such hits as “This Magic Moment,” “Viva Las Vegas,” and “Save the Last Dance for Me.” Doc Pomus, born Jerome Solon Felder, was a foundational figure in rock ’n’ roll and R&B during the mid-20th century, influencing generations of artists. His music was recorded by such notables as Ray Charles, the Drifters, Dion, Big Joe Turner and Elvis Presley. The collection, which will be held by the Library’s National Audio-Visual Conservation Center, includes more than 450 non-commercial recordings of song demos, working tapes, interviews, performances and conversations, as well as lyric manuscripts, journals, notebooks, essays, liner notes and more. title: David Schmitz named director and chief curator of Iowa State University Museums
summary: David Schmitz has been named the next Warren and Beverly Madden Endowed Director and Chief Curator of University Museums at Iowa State University. The appointment follows a national search and took effect July 13. “David was chosen from a talented and accomplished candidate pool and comes to us with 20 years in the museum and cultural arts field. He is a proven director, fundraiser, curator, and collaborator,” said Duane Reeves, Assistant Vice President for Specialty Business Services and Cultural Arts. David is not a newcomer here. He joined University Museums as Interim Academic Engagement Coordinator in December 2025. In that advisory role, he collaborated with staff, faculty, and campus partners to envision how the museums' collections and exhibitions can further enhance student learning, engagement, and success. title: Archives of 1930s Japanese psychic experiments featured in new MoNTUE exhibition
summary: Curated by Alice Nien-pu Ko, Remote Viewing takes as its point of departure a 1930s Japanese experiment that attempted to transmit an image of the moon’s far side onto a photographic plate through mental projection. Tomokichi Fukurai, the psychologist and psychical researcher who played a critical role in this experiment, worked at the nexus of an international movement investigating the hidden capacities of the mind, bringing a distinctly Asian perspective to the field. Although professionally ostracized for his work, the striking photographs produced through these experiments remain a testament to Fukurai’s radical proposal that the mind as a form of imaging technology is relevant to creation today. Presented through an art-historical lens, these previously unexhibited photographs open onto the exhibition’s broader inquiry into the mind as an imaging apparatus. title: The National Museum of Art, Osaka presents Aki Sasamoto's 'Life Laboratory'
summary: The National Museum of Art, Osaka is presenting the special exhibition Aki Sasamoto’s Life Laboratory. Based on the exhibition held at the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo in 2025, this presentation has been partly reconfigured to include works from the museum’s collection. Sasamoto continually alternates between sculptural thinking and bodily expression. Combining elements such as string, tubing, everyday objects, sound, and language, she constructs installations that function like circuits through which thoughts and emotions circulate. By entering these spaces herself and performing through speech and movement, she treats each work as not a fixed object but an event that continues to evolve over time. title: 1888 Proof Double Eagle leads Heritage's Summer FUN U.S. Coins Auction to $12.4 million
summary: An extraordinary 1888 Double Eagle, PR64 Deep Cameo PCGS sold for $170,800 to lead Heritage’s July 16-18 Summer FUN U.S. Coins Signature® Auction to $12,400,954. The proof double eagle topped an expansive offering of more than 1,400 lots spanning the breadth of American numismatics, establishing a new auction record for an 1888 in the PR64 Deep Cameo grade. An 1861-S Paquet Double Eagle, AU55 NGC from The Fudd Collection finished at $128,100 to claim the event’s second-highest result. The 1888 double eagle came from a proof mintage of either 102 or 105 pieces, of which an estimated 20 to 25 survive in all grades. Struck during the Gilded Age, the coin features glassy orange-gold mirrored fields surrounding richly frosted devices. Its smooth, watery fields distinguish it from some other 1888 proofs that exhibit an “orange-peel” texture caused by differences in planchet annealing. title: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts receives $1.5 million donation for contemporary art fund
summary: Great news for local contemporary art: the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts Foundation announced a remarkable donation of $1.5 million by patrons Danielle Lysaught and Paul Hamelin. Made as part of the major fundraising campaign The Museum Transforms Lives (2023–2028), this donation will endow the Hamelys Fund for Contemporary Quebec and Canadian Art. As philanthropists who are deeply committed to their community, Danielle Lysaught and Paul Hamelin are particularly interested in the visual arts, education and health fields. They are the founders of Projet Casa, a space for contemporary art exhibitions by emerging or unrepresented artists. title: Artpace announces 2028 Texas Open Call, application fee waived for Texas artists
summary: Artpace San Antonio is now accepting applications for the 2028 Texas Open Call, the primary pathway for Texas-based artists to be considered for Artpace's International Artist-in-Residence program and for studio visits from curators in Artpace's Curatorial Residency program. The application period opened on Monday, July 13, and closes Monday, August 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM CST. Applications are submitted online at AnyArtist.org. To limit financial barriers and make the process more accessible, Artpace is waiving application fees for the 2028 Texas Open Call. title: BEERS London presents Andrew Salgado's first series of abstract florals
summary: BEERS London is presenting a new body of work by Andrew Salgado, entitled Glory! For the first time, Salgado ventures from figurative painting to present a series devoted exclusively to abstracted florals. At once funereal and joyous, these exuberant compositions occupy a space between celebration and mourning, expression and uncertainty. Bursting with colour and vitality, they embrace contradiction: frustration and release, restraint and abandon, beauty and decay. For the artist, the word "glory" is laden with possibility, at once promising and mildly unsettling; its etymology meaning majestic and light, but also heaviness, social weightiness. Given the turmoil of recent years, as well as Salgado's own increasingly literary approach to his art, this body of work is a response and reaction to his own tendency toward narrative. title: Landscape exhibition at Flowers Gallery explores real and reimagined natural worlds
summary: In the canon of Western art, the landscape is among the most traditional of subjects. This exhibition brings together work embracing the traditions of landscape painting, using the natural world to construct images that are both real and reimagined within the artists’ unique visual languages. Tai Shan Schierenberg, William Crozier and Lucy Jones explore the boundaries of colour to enrich their paintings with unexpected bursts and flashes of paint, the vivid hues seemingly conveying an emotive response rather than a true rendition of the subject. In Tom Phillips’s Road to Alice Springs, 2012, his jewel-like collage is evocative of the area’s climate, appearing as if the heat is shimmering back at the viewer, the fragmented shards of colour configured to create an abstracted mirage. title: Andrew Bannecker brings color and joy to 2026 National Book Festival Poster
summary: The Library of Congress unveiled the 2026 Library of Congress National Book Festival poster, designed by acclaimed illustrator and designer Andrew Bannecker, best known for his vibrant, highly stylized illustrations that combine bold colors, intricate patterns and emotional storytelling. From his work with global brands and major media outlets to cultural institutions and even the British Royal Mail, the Kansas-born illustrator has said his goal isn’t attention but “connection,” and it shows in his award-winning work spanning more than two decades. Bannecker’s poster celebrates the transformative power of reading through his signature vibrant and richly layered work. title: New museum at Kabah explores two decades of Maya research in Yucatán's Puuc region
summary: A new museum devoted to the archaeology, history and living culture of the Maya has opened at the Kabah Archaeological Zone in Yucatán, bringing together more than 250 objects and the results of two decades of research across the Puuc region. The Puuc Archaeological Museum was developed by Mexico’s Ministry of Culture through the National Institute of Anthropology and History, known as INAH, with a total investment of approximately 227 million pesos. The project included the construction and outfitting of the museum, as well as a new visitor services facility at the archaeological site. Located near some of the most important ancient Maya cities in the region—including Uxmal, Sayil, Labná and Xlapak—the museum is intended to offer visitors a broader understanding of the societies that shaped the Puuc landscape.

title: Serpentine South opens interactive archive display on art and advanced technology
summary: Serpentine is presenting processing… an open-access archive display, sharing the experimental methodologies and creative research and development (R&D) that has shaped its pioneering work at the intersection of art and advanced technologies. The display is presented in the Education Space, Serpentine South, from 20 July to 6 September 2026. This summer, Serpentine’s Education Space has been transformed into an active archive, listening room and research space. This display marks a significant moment in the preservation and activation of Serpentine’s pioneering work with art and advanced technologies - which today includes artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain and game engines. processing… takes its name from the familiar message shown during an in-progress computation, evoking a state of continual activity and change. title: Nardeen Srouji exhibition at CCA explores architecture, land, and memory
summary: Two cypress trees stand at the entrance to the Center for Contemporary Art building. The metallic structure, with its postmodern architectural language, and the pair of evergreens, form the point of departure for Nardeen Srouji's (b. 1980, Nazareth) exhibition. Through them, the artist reflects on the place in which she is exhibiting, the land on which it stands, and the surrounding historical, political, social, and physical layers—houses and building materials, neighborhoods that have been erased, traces that have been assimilated into the landscape, ornamental motifs, and vegetation. The exhibition spans the gallery's two spaces and includes a site-specific installation and embroidery works. title: ICA San José affiliated artist, Miguel Novelo, selected as 2026 Artadia Awardee
summary: The Institute of Contemporary Art San José (ICA) congratulates exhibiting artist Miguel Novelo on being named a 2026 San Francisco Bay Area Artadia Awardee. The honor comes during Novelo’s presentation at the ICA San José, on view through August 23, 2026, and follows his selection as a 2026 Knight Arts + Tech Fellow earlier this year. Artadia selected Novelo, alongside Morehshin Allahyari and Maya Fuji, as recipients of the 2026 San Francisco Bay Area Artadia. The three awardees were chosen from a distinguished group of finalists that also included Mark Baugh-Sasaki, Soleé Darrell, and Daniel Arthur Mendoza. The award recognizes artists whose work demonstrates exceptional artistic merit and supports their continued practice efforts through unrestricted funding. title: Barber Institute transformation project underway
summary: A once-in-a-generation transformation of the Barber Institute of Fine Arts, University of Birmingham is underway following a successful £14.8million fundraising campaign. As part of an ambitious project to make the building more accessible and welcoming and enhance the presentation of art and music for all, a wide-ranging scheme of improvements is now in progress. A ramp and accessible ground-floor entrance are currently being installed at the side of the Grade-1 listed building on the University’s Edgbaston campus, while the terrace is also being enlarged.
